sample.question:
Tower of Hanoi is a classic puzzle with three pegs labeled A, B and C (left to right) and several disks of different sizes. Disks are numbered by size: disk 1 is the smallest. A disk's number is printed on it. Only the TOP disk of a peg can be moved, and it may only be placed on an empty peg or on top of a LARGER disk. The move X->Y means: take the top disk of peg X and put it on peg Y.

Starting from the position in the image, the following moves are attempted one by one: A->A, C->A, C->C, C->B, B->B. An ILLEGAL move (from an empty peg, onto a smaller disk, or onto the same peg) is skipped and changes nothing. After the whole sequence, on which peg is disk 2? Answer with the peg letter.
sample.analysis:
Initial position: peg A: disks [1] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [5, 4, 2] (bottom to top); peg C: disks [3] (bottom to top).
Move 1 (A->A): ILLEGAL - source and target are the same peg; the move is skipped and nothing changes.
Move 2 (C->A): ILLEGAL - disk 3 cannot rest on the smaller disk 1; the move is skipped and nothing changes.
Move 3 (C->C): ILLEGAL - source and target are the same peg; the move is skipped and nothing changes.
Move 4 (C->B): ILLEGAL - disk 3 cannot rest on the smaller disk 2; the move is skipped and nothing changes.
Move 5 (B->B): ILLEGAL - source and target are the same peg; the move is skipped and nothing changes.
Final position: peg A: disks [1] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [5, 4, 2] (bottom to top); peg C: disks [3] (bottom to top).
Disk 2 ends on peg B.
So the answer is B.
